questions.q: What has the city become like even though she was once great among the nations?
questions.a: The city has become like a widow, alone and without protection.

questions.q: What can Judah not find even though she lives among the nations?
questions.a: Judah can find no rest even though she lives among the nations.
Yahweh has afflicted Jerusalem because of her many transgressions.

questions.q: What has left the daughter of Zion?
questions.a: All of her majesty and beauty have left the daughter of Zion.

questions.q: What did Jerusalem remember in the days of her affliction?
questions.a: Jerusalem remembered all of her precious things that she had in former times.

questions.q: Because Jerusalem sinned greatly, what is the result?
questions.a: Jerusalem is now regarded as something abhorrent and defiled.

questions.q: Who has Jerusalem seen enter her sanctuary even though Yahweh commanded that they must not enter?
questions.a: Jerusalem has seen the nations enter her sanctuary.

questions.q: What do the people do as they search for bread?
questions.a: The people groan as they search for bread.

questions.q: What has Yahweh spread for the feet of Jerusalem?
questions.a: Yahweh has spread a net for the feet of Jerusalem.

questions.q: What is the result of the God placing the yoke of Jerusalem’s transgressions on her neck?
questions.a: The result is that Jerusalem’s strength has stumbled and they are given into the hands of their enemies.

questions.q: What has the Lord done to the virgin daughter of Judah?
questions.a: The Lord has crushed the people of Judah like someone treading on grapes in a winepress.

questions.q: Why have Jerusalem’s children become desolate?
questions.a: Jerusalem’s children have become desolate because the enemy has prevailed.

questions.q: Who has gone into captivity because Jerusalem rebelled against Yahweh’s commands?
questions.a: Jerusalem’s young women and young men have gone into captivity.

questions.q: Who died in the city while they sought food to restore their lives?
questions.a: Jerusalem’s priests and elders died in the city.

questions.q: What is the result of Jerusalem’s rebellion?
questions.a: Jerusalem is in anguish and their hearts are completely devastated.

questions.q: What do the enemies of Jerusalem do when they hear of her calamity?
What does Jerusalem request that Yahweh do to her enemies?
questions.a: Jerusalem asks that Yahweh would deal with her enemies just as Yahweh has dealt with her for all her transgressions.

commentary.text: The miserable state of Jerusalem, the just consequences of its sins. (Lam. 1:1-11) Jerusalem represented as a captive female, lamenting, and seeking the mercy of God. (Lam. 1:12-22)

Lam. 1:1-11 The prophet sometimes speaks in his own person; at other times Jerusalem, as a distressed female, is the speaker, or some of the Jews. The description shows the miseries of the Jewish nation. Jerusalem became a captive and a slave, by reason of the greatness of her sins; and had no rest from suffering. If we allow sin, our greatest adversary, to have dominion over us, justly will other enemies also be suffered to have dominion. The people endured the extremities of famine and distress. In this sad condition Jerusalem acknowledged her sin, and entreated the Lord to look upon her case. This is the only way to make ourselves easy under our burdens; for it is the just anger of the Lord for man's transgressions, that has filled the earth with sorrows, lamentations, sickness, and death.

Lam. 1:12-22 Jerusalem, sitting dejected on the ground, calls on those that passed by, to consider whether her example did not concern them. Her outward sufferings were great, but her inward sufferings were harder to bear, through the sense of guilt. Sorrow for sin must be great sorrow, and must affect the soul. Here we see the evil of sin, and may take warning to flee from the wrath to come. Whatever may be learned from the sufferings of Jerusalem, far more may be learned from the sufferings of Christ. Does he not from the cross speak to every one of us? Does he not say, Is it nothing to you, all ye that pass by? Let all our sorrows lead us to the cross of Christ, lead us to mark his example, and cheerfully to follow him.
